llm_evidence_note: No model is called. The real native ctx.terminals PTY seam (reused committed B3 runtime role) is driven through a minimal BYQ-owned TerminalAttachment adapter plus B4 reconcile; this is terminal-attachment-continuity evidence, NOT real-LLM-quality evidence.

ownership.rule: BYQ owns ONLY the bounded TerminalAttachment lifecycle (BYQ-minted attachment id, owner principal/authorization, runtime generation, executor epoch, state, audit) and orphan reconcile. DSH owns the PTY/shell/process/IO. BYQ must not build a PTY runtime, must not copy a DSH terminal, must not build a second generic harness and must not persist or fake the native PTY.

required_scenarios.description: generation A establishes a real native persistent terminal plus a durable BYQ TerminalAttachment. The DSH runtime OS process is genuinely terminated (old PTY pid dies) and a fresh runtime OS process generation B is started. A fresh adapter generation B reloads the SAME durable attachment, performs owner authorization and generation/epoch validation, finds the native process-local state genuinely unreachable, deterministically records lost/interrupted and rejects a fake reattach. Per ADR-0083 this honest loss is the acceptance.

the native DSH state (a real PTY) genuinely SURVIVES while the BYQ durable attachment record is lost. A fresh adapter generation B reconciles the native sessions against the durable attachments, detects the surviving PTY as an orphan, classifies it lost, and NEVER silently reuses or adopts it; the stale attachment id is rejected and cleanup ends the orphan PTY with no orphans left.

optional_scenarios.description: host reboot. NOT executed: rebooting the maintainer host is not authorized and a container/process restart is not a host reboot.

required_cross_checks.description: the BYQ attachment is a real durable, BYQ-minted record distinct from any DSH session id or pid: it persists to a BYQ-owned store, carries owner principal + runtime generation + executor epoch + state + audit linkage, and reloads with the same id in a fresh adapter OS process

the DSH runtime OS process was genuinely terminated and restarted: a different runtime OS pid, an advanced runtime generation, the generation-A PTY pid really gone and the new runtime holding no sessions
an owner/principal boundary cannot be bypassed: a foreign principal presenting the attachment is rejected, and a different native owner cannot read or send to another owner's PTY
a stale runtime generation / executor epoch is fenced before any rebind or reconcile decision, in both the DSH-restart and orphan worlds
an unknown/wrong attachment or terminal id is rejected and cannot reach a real PTY
the honest loss is stable across retries: a repeated reattach returns the same lost state, orphan reconcile is idempotent and closing twice is a no-op
closing the attachment / restarting the runtime and the orphan cleanup leave no orphan PTY process
terminal (attachment/PTY) lifetime never defines conversation or durable-job lifetime: BYQ conversation/job identities survive both the DSH runtime restart and the orphan loss unchanged and active

notes.native_seam: the real native @deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal service + @deepseek-ai/dsh-terminal-bash backend own the PTY/shell/IO; the committed B3 harness runtime role is reused unchanged. A minimal B4 BYQ adapter owns only the durable TerminalAttachment lifecycle and orphan reconcile. No PTY runtime, no second generic harness, no DSH fork/patch.
notes.dsh_runtime_restart: the DSH runtime OS process is SIGKILLed and a genuinely fresh OS process is started as the next runtime generation. Native sessions are process-local, so the old PTY dies with the runtime; the honest result is lost/interrupted, never a fabricated reattach.
notes.surviving_pty: a real PTY surviving without any BYQ attachment is an orphan; reconcile classifies it lost and never silently reuses it.
notes.lifetime_independence: terminal lifetime never defines conversation or durable-job lifetime; the BYQ conversation/job identities survive terminal loss.
